economic_impact.status_label: Rapid sectoral assessment ongoing; no official monetary loss estimate available

known_impacts.status: 200 BTS/sites disrupted across 10 districts/cities involving three operators; restoration monitored by Komdigi.
Damage reported at 5 airports and 2 ports (Reo Port and Maumere/Laurentius Say Port); named facilities include Laurentius Say Port, Reo Port, Nangakeo Port and Komodo Airport.
known_impacts.confidence: Official Ministry of Transportation statement; corroborated by BNPB and media reporting of '5 bandara dan 2 pelabuhan'

known_impacts.status: Pioneer service at Nangakeo Port temporarily suspended; Komodo Airport continued operating normally with restrictions.
Landslides and rockfall disrupted several routes; consolidated road-damage and reopening status remain under assessment.
known_impacts.confidence: BNPB and forwarded Basarnas field reporting

known_impacts.status: PLN reported 88% of affected customers in Flores had power restored as of its early-morning 16 August briefing (Darmawan Prasodjo, PLN President Director). All 11 affected primary substations (100%) and 58 of 59 feeders (98.3%) were back in operation; 2,723 of 3,478 affected distribution substations, serving roughly 441,000 customers, were restored as of an earlier 15 August, 18:30 WITA update. Repairs are concentrated on landslide-affected areas where poles collapsed. Hospitals (e.g. RSUD Bajawa) and airports were prioritised.
known_impacts.confidence: Official PLN statement (Direktur Utama PT PLN, Darmawan Prasodjo; General Manager PLN UIW NTT, F. Eko Sulistyono)

known_impacts.status: One Bulog warehouse was reported affected; operational and stock-loss details remain under verification.
Pertamina temporarily suspended operations at a number of fuel stations (SPBU) in the affected area as a safety precaution; scope and duration not detailed in sources reviewed.
known_impacts.confidence: Media reporting (Liputan6), not yet corroborated by an official Pertamina statement located in this update

child_protection.status_label: NGO response update — Save the Children Indonesia (SCIDN), 15 August 2026

headline.children_affected_note: SCIDN reports more than 8,000 children in NTT facing disrupted education and heightened protection risks. This is an NGO field estimate, not a BNPB or Ministry of Social Affairs figure, and is shown separately.

compounding_hazards.status_label: The earthquake response is layered on pre-existing regional hazards
hazards: Recurring eruption hazard from Mount Lewotobi
compounding_hazards.note: SCIDN's update frames the earthquake as compounding these existing vulnerabilities rather than an isolated event, with cumulative effects on health, protection, education, psychosocial well-being and long-term child development.

priority_response_sectors.focus: Preventing violence, exploitation and family separation; monitoring unaccompanied children, family tracing and reunification, institutionalisation/orphanage risk, and heightened child-trafficking risk during disasters.
Ensuring continuous, safe learning for every child given severe disruption at damaged education facilities.
Critical care focused on children aged 0-23 months and pregnant/lactating mothers.
Helping children process trauma, build resilience and cope with distress.
Preventing disease outbreaks in evacuation sites and temporary shelters.

child_protection.response_status: SCIDN has established contact with CIS Timor in NTT; a joint assessment has been agreed to gather detailed data on children's needs and vulnerabilities to guide priority response actions.
